rules: Urban Farm – Class B (may be in a greenhouse) is a conditional use in I-2
physics: root-zone heating at about 38 °C takes low-grade heat; pipe-rail heating at 82 °C needs a heat pump
land: little yard left: a rooftop greenhouse or a neighbour's lot
demand: the heat offered could warm about 5,561–13,059 m² of greenhouse at 1.63–2.1 GJ/m² a year (Ontario, Manitoba measured); BC vegetable greenhouses use 1.3–2.0 GJ/m² a year of all energy (industry estimate, 2011). For scale: the City of Vancouver has 3 greenhouse farms (area not published); BC has about 5.9 million m² (Census of Agriculture 2021)
time: greenhouses need most heat in winter nights, as data centres give it all year; and in BC from May to October 90% of greenhouse gas is burned for its CO₂, not its heat — about half the year's gas — so server heat replaces only part of it (BC Greenhouse Sector report, 2011)
money: Alberta greenhouses in 2023: investment $105–478 per m² by crop, natural gas $4–12 per m² a year (the heat a data centre could displace); about 85% heat with natural gas (Alberta Agriculture and Irrigation, 2023 survey of 53 growers; no BC figure). What a grower would pay for server heat is not published

rules: Metro Vancouver gives access first come, first served, with a letter of support (UT-008)
land: per-pipe flow near the parcel is not published
demand: a rival source for the same receivers, not a receiver

physics: a data centre rejects heat; giving cooling needs a chiller and a pipe
demand: 3 cooling towers with active City operating permits within 500 m — buildings that already make their own cooling (City open data, 2026)
